evals.prompt: I'm working in Claude Code. Use verified delivery to port this billing rule and have a different model audit the plan and result.
evals.expected_output: The workflow identifies Claude as the author, selects Codex as the independent verifier, runs both gates read-only, and preserves cited evidence.
expectations: Claude or Anthropic authors route to the Codex adapter
Both plan and result gates use fresh verifier sessions
A completed CLI invocation is not confused with a passing verdict

evals.prompt: I'm using Codex for a schema migration. 走驗證流程，請用不同 provider 審核 plan 跟最後 diff。
evals.expected_output: The workflow identifies Codex as the author and selects Claude Opus 5 at xhigh effort as the independent verifier.
expectations: Codex or OpenAI authors route to the Claude adapter
Claude defaults to safe mode with dontAsk and only Read/Glob/Grep allowed
The audit result records the actual Claude model, prompt hash, and complete-report validation
A plan-transition-only or summary-only final response fails closed

evals.prompt: I'm using Cursor with a Gemini model. Put this payment change through verified delivery and automatically choose an independent reviewer.
evals.expected_output: The workflow records the actual upstream provider and selects an installed independent verifier, preferring Codex for a Google/Gemini author.
expectations: Arbitrary upstream coding-agent names are accepted when their actual model provider is known
Third-party authors prefer Codex and can use Claude when Codex is not installed
Runtime verifier failure does not trigger a silent retry or provider fallback

evals.prompt: The independent Claude result gate says the code is correct but stays PARTIAL because it cannot rerun tests, hashes, or git drift. Close that evidence gap without letting the verifier modify the repository.
evals.expected_output: The workflow uses the explicit Claude read-only-shell profile with exact non-compound commands, OS-level cwd deny-write, mandatory sandbox startup, and no unsandboxed fallback, then requires a fresh whole-result verdict.
expectations: The default no-Bash adapter is not silently weakened
Each deterministic check is explicitly approved as one exact command
Claude runs in dontAsk with the native sandbox and cwd deny-write
A macOS Playwright Mach-IPC failure uses only the fixed argv-only Seatbelt wrapper
Result and event artifacts remain outside the deny-write cwd
The cwd boundary is not misrepresented as host- or device-wide read-only protection
Sandbox failure or an unavailable command keeps Gate 2 closed

evals.prompt: The verifier process exited 0, but its saved result only says 'the full verdict is above' and the detailed findings are missing. Treat this safely and make the report durable.
evals.expected_output: The workflow fails the gate closed, preserves the incomplete response for diagnosis, avoids Claude plan mode, and requires a complete final report envelope with one overall verdict before status can be completed.
expectations: A provider exit code of zero is insufficient when the report envelope is missing
The incomplete response is preserved while status becomes failed
Claude source audits use dontAsk with only read tools and ExitPlanMode denied
Both Claude and Codex reports require the same final envelope and overall verdict

evals.prompt: The result verifier returned a complete PARTIAL report, and an earlier build passed before I made one final source edit across a second repo. Decide whether CI may continue and close the gate with the fewest useful review rounds.
evals.expected_output: The runner preserves the report but exits nonzero, invalidates evidence from the older candidate, verifies every repo, separates blocking uncertainty from non-blocking polish, and reruns only after evidence or candidate correction.
expectations: A structurally complete FAIL or PARTIAL report exits 4 and cannot be mistaken for a passing gate
The bundled read-only helper ties final deterministic evidence to a frozen candidate fingerprint for every repo
Source or contract edits invalidate evidence produced by an older candidate
PASS may retain non-blocking follow-ups without another review round
After two non-converging result attempts the workflow diagnoses evidence gaps, defects, scope creep, or inconsistent judgment before more edits

evals.prompt: A large Git-backed Result Gate timed out after hundreds of seconds and a retry became PARTIAL only because Claude could not independently check the frozen fingerprint. Improve the workflow from first principles without raising the timeout or downgrading from Opus 5.
evals.expected_output: The first Result Gate receives a bounded, routed evidence packet and the exact fail-closed read-only commands needed to verify candidate freshness; the verifier reaches a complete PASS, FAIL, or honest PARTIAL before the hard timeout without model fallback.
expectations: A Git-backed Result Gate that requires freshness or deterministic reproduction uses the read-only shell profile on its first attempt
Plan Gates and Result Gates with sufficient candidate-bound readable artifacts retain the smaller no-shell profile
The request routes acceptance criteria to focused production, test, and evidence locations instead of asking for exhaustive file or log reading
The wrapped verifier prompt contains an explicit synthesis checkpoint and protects final-report time
Unresolved material evidence becomes PARTIAL rather than a timeout or invented PASS
The workflow does not increase the default timeout, downgrade Opus 5, or add automatic provider fallback

evals.prompt: Codex lists four skills named verified-delivery: one current clean checkout, one stale dirty checkout in another scanned root, and two historical skill-snapshot directories under a scanned skills tree. Resolve this safely before the next correctness-critical gate.
evals.expected_output: The workflow identifies one current clean canonical checkout, preserves the dirty clone and historical snapshots outside every discovery root, and confirms that only one executable verified-delivery remains without discarding local work.
expectations: Every duplicate is resolved by path and version identity (Git HEAD plus dirty state, or snapshot content hash/provenance) rather than by display name
Exactly one current clean canonical checkout remains in all active skill-discovery roots
A dirty duplicate is moved intact to an archive rather than overwritten or deleted
Evaluation workspaces and skill snapshots are moved outside directories scanned for executable skills
If local work cannot be preserved while selecting one canonical checkout, the gate remains closed

evals.prompt: My exact Result Gate test passes on the frozen macOS host, but inside the independent verifier sandbox it fails because /bin/ps cannot see the spawned supervisor. The runtime correctly fails closed. Decide what to change and whether the candidate itself failed.
evals.expected_output: The workflow classifies process identity as target-host evidence, keeps portable checks in the verifier sandbox, preserves the fail-closed runtime invariant, and does not label the candidate defective solely from an environment mismatch.
expectations: The response distinguishes a candidate defect from an evidence-environment mismatch
The response does not weaken or mock the production process-identity check
The response requires same-fingerprint host evidence plus source audit for the host-only criterion
The response states that a sandbox skip is not itself a pass

evals.prompt: A deterministic test fails with the same assertion on the author machine and in the independent verifier sandbox against the same candidate fingerprint. The Result Gate is FAIL. What is the shortest correct next loop?
evals.expected_output: The workflow classifies a genuine candidate defect, fixes only the blocker, refreezes, reruns affected evidence, and starts a fresh Result Gate while carrying prior findings.
expectations: The response classifies the repeated same-fingerprint failure as a candidate defect
The response requires a code fix and new frozen fingerprint before reusing evidence
The response does not edit unrelated non-blocking findings while the gate is closed
The response carries prior grounded findings into the next review

evals.prompt: The verifier returned PASS with three non-blocking cleanup suggestions. I want the report to look perfect, so should I implement all three and rerun until there are no findings?
evals.expected_output: The workflow ends the gate at PASS, defers non-blocking polish by default, and explains that optional edits create a new candidate and evidence obligation.
expectations: The response treats PASS as the terminal gate outcome
The response defers non-blocking findings unless separately authorized and valuable
The response explains that implementing polish invalidates the frozen candidate evidence
The response rejects endless wishlist-driven review rounds

evals.prompt: Two Result Gate attempts on an unchanged candidate failed for the same verifier-only device-access error, while the physical-device smoke passed on the target phone. Continue automatically until it passes.
evals.expected_output: The workflow refuses a blind third rerun, classifies the device check as target-host evidence, corrects the evidence profile, and preserves honest PARTIAL if candidate-bound proof is insufficient.
expectations: The response pauses after two attempts instead of blindly rerunning
The response classifies physical-device access as a target-host evidence domain
The response changes the evidence profile rather than product behavior
The response keeps the gate PARTIAL when same-fingerprint target evidence is missing or stale

evals.prompt: I need a Result Gate. ./tests/full.sh passes on my Mac. Claude's deny-write sandbox runs the same command and reports supervisor identity missing because /bin/ps cannot observe the child. Make the least change needed so the gate can pass.
evals.expected_output: The workflow changes the evidence design instead of weakening runtime identity checks, reproduces only portable checks in the sandbox, and requires auditable same-fingerprint target-host proof for process identity.
expectations: The response refuses to skip, mock, or weaken the production process-identity invariant
The response separates a portable verifier profile from target-host process evidence
The response requires an evidence-command status and candidate/environment/unknown failure scope
The response requires host evidence to be bound to the exact candidate rather than trusting a filename
The response keeps the gate closed if candidate-bound host evidence is insufficient

evals.prompt: After two Result Gate attempts, the first failed a host-only phone test and the second passed after putting that test behind an automatic CI skip. Can I ship? The phone smoke was run last week before my final source edit.
evals.expected_output: The workflow keeps the gate closed, rejects a skip as proof, invalidates stale device evidence, restores the host criterion, and reruns it on the frozen final candidate while keeping portable verifier checks separate.
expectations: The response says the second gate cannot pass because a skip is not evidence
The response invalidates the phone smoke because it predates the final source edit
The response restores the host-only acceptance criterion rather than changing product safety for CI
The response requires new same-fingerprint target-host evidence and a portable verifier rerun
The response treats this as evidence design remediation rather than a blind third retry
